text:
deploy-bot: [deploy-notice] Attempted promote: release rc4 (build 2026-03-20-rc4) -> prod. Compliance gate FAILED: SCA_SCAN_HIGH (1 high severity finding). Blocking promote.

deploy-bot: SBOM excerpt:
```
- package: pkg:github/fastparse/libfastparse@1.2.3
  - dependency path: redwood-optimizer -> fastparse
  - finding: CVE-2025-4823 (high) - unsafe parsing leads to RCE in some configs
  - remediation: upgrade to libfastparse@1.2.4 or apply CONFIG_SAFE_PARSING=true
```

alana: @sec-eng ack. Quick q — is this externally exploitable in our default prod config?

sec-eng: short: low in default but not zero. Exploit requires user-controlled uploads + certain plugin enabled. We do have a handful of customers with that plugin on. Patch available upstream 1.2.4. Mitigation: set CONFIG_SAFE_PARSING=true and add WAF rule for payload size/regex.

jamie: options: 1) rebuild rc4 with libfastparse pinned to 1.1.9 (known-good) and retest (~45m), 2) rebuild with 1.2.4 and run CI (~30-40m), 3) rollback to 2026-03-19-stable (fast).

mike: change window closes 23:00 PDT. Current time ~21:15. If rebuild/retest pushes past window we lose deploy today. Given customer risk + window, rollback seems safest.

alana: any customers on Dedicated or Private who would notice rollback? Could break DB migrations?

jamie: rollback to 2026-03-19-stable is a straight promote, no DB schema changes. Dedicated customers unaffected (they're pinned to dedicated builds). Only hosted users get the change.

sec-eng: we can approve an emergency exception if we flip CONFIG_SAFE_PARSING and add a short-term WAF rule, but that needs a support ticket and product sign-off. That still leaves the vulnerability present (mitigated). Full remediation requires upstream patch or internal patch.

product-ops-bot: created RF-2145: "rc4-blocked-by-supply-chain-finding" -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RF-2145 (assign: @jamie, priority: P0 for patch + release notes)

deploy-bot: promote paused. React with :eyes: when you've reviewed. If no explicit approval by 22:00 PDT we'll auto-initiate rollback to last stable.

mike: +1 to rollback. I'll trigger the rollback now.

deploy-bot: Running rollback -> promote 2026-03-19-stable to prod. Command: `deploy promote --to 2026-03-19-stable --env prod --reason "sbom-scan-fail"`

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. Prod back to 2026-03-19-stable. Canary reopened at 21:45. No downtime observed.

alana: I'll update the release notes and customer comms. Add note: blocked by supply-chain finding (CVE-2025-4823), mitigation steps & ETA for patched release.

jamie: I'll start rebuild pipeline using libfastparse@1.2.4 and run the full regression. ETA ~40m. Will update RF-2145 with artifacts.

sec-eng: follow-up actions: (1) add SBOM check to pre-promote hook to fail earlier in CI, (2) add automatic config flip suggestion in the deploy UI when sca high found, (3) schedule a sweep of customers using the plugin.

deploy-bot: Note: gate logs saved to /var/logs/deploy/gates/1779002345-sca.json

mike: thanks team. Postmortem please include timeline + why the SBOM check passed earlier but flagged on promote (we're missing a transitive lock in build).

alana: noted. I'll own the postmortem and the customer comms. Tagging @sec-eng and @jamie for remediation steps. :thumbsup:
